mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening economy, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST shows a sustained 3-month increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over the previous 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently, negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous 3 months signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.5% over the previous 3 months, it signals a robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% and UNRATE decrease > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% over the previous 3 months, it signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 2% in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances where PAYEMS shows a sustained 3-month increase.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) increases by more than 2% and housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% over the previous 6 months, it signals a strong demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase > 2% and HOUST increase > 5% in 6 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where both conditions are met.
